title: The north-east
subtitle: Veneto, Friuli and the Alps
objectives: Explain how the Alps shape the north-east

steps.title: The Veneto
steps.body: The Veneto makes more wine than almost any other Italian region. Valpolicella, near Verona, uses Corvina for light reds, Ripasso and Amarone. Soave, east of Verona, uses Garganega. Prosecco is made from Glera across the Veneto and Friuli. Lake Garda tempers the western side, where Bardolino and Lugana grow.

steps.title: The Alps' influence
steps.body: The Alps protect the north-east from cold northern winds, while their cool air flows down valleys at night, keeping acidity high. In Alto Adige, vineyards climb from 200 to over 1,000 m, growing Pinot Grigio, Gewürztraminer and the red Lagrein. Friuli, near Slovenia, makes crisp whites from Friulano, Pinot Grigio and Ribolla Gialla.
steps.highlight: Mountain air keeps the wines fresh

steps.prompt: Match each wine to its region.
steps.explanation: Each north-eastern region has its own grapes.

steps.title: Orange wines and skin contact
steps.body: In Friuli, near the Slovenian border, producers like Josko Gravner revived long skin contact for white grapes in the 1990s, sometimes in Georgian qvevri. Ribolla Gialla and Friulano became amber, tannic wines. Friuli's Collio and Colli Orientali are now reference areas for this style, alongside Slovenia's Brda.
steps.highlight: Friuli: home of modern orange wine

steps.prompt: Alto Adige has vineyards above 1,000 metres.
steps.explanation: Yes. Its mountain vineyards climb from about 200 m to over 1,000 m, keeping wines fresh and aromatic.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The Veneto makes Valpolicella, Soave and Prosecco
The Alps keep Alto Adige and Friuli fresh
Friuli is a reference for modern orange wine
